title: LabPdfExtraction

BBox.description:
A rectangle on a page, in PDF points.

Coordinate convention, matching the doc-factory's recorded convention
exactly (`agent/evals/w2/factory/groundtruth.py` COORDINATE_CONVENTION)
so that ground truth and extractor output are directly comparable:
origin top-left, y increasing downward — PyMuPDF page space, on the
original clean layout rather than on a degraded scan.

`x1 >= x0` and `y1 >= y0`, not `>`: a zero-width box is real data. The
factory emits one for every unflagged lab result (an empty flag column
renders as `[306.0, 256.398, 306.0, 268.24]`), and rejecting it would
make the contract unable to describe a normal lab row.

page.description: 1-based page number within the source document.
page.title: Page

x0.description: Left edge, PDF points from the page's left edge.
x0.title: X0

y0.description: Top edge, PDF points from the page's top edge (y down).
y0.title: Y0

BBox.title: BBox

Citation.description:
One citation. CLAUDE.md invariant 2's five fields, plus the two the
document case needs. See the module docstring for the rules.

source_type.description: Which kind of source this points at. Invariant 3: chart facts and guideline evidence are distinct kinds and never substitute for one another.

source_id.description: chart: the FHIR resource id, exactly Week 1's Claim.source_id. document: the stored document's id. guideline: the guideline document's id.
source_id.title: Source Id

page_or_section.description: chart: the tool-scope resource type this fact came from, one of CHART_SECTIONS — a chart has no pages, so its 'section' is which part of the record it is. document: the page, as a string; when it parses as an integer it must equal bbox.page. guideline: the section heading the chunk sits under. Required for document and guideline.
page_or_section.title: Page Or Section

field_or_chunk_id.description: chart: the field name on the source resource (Week 1's Claim.field). document: the extracted field's path, in the doc-factory's field_path vocabulary. guideline: the retrieved chunk's id.
field_or_chunk_id.title: Field Or Chunk Id

quote_or_value.description: What the source holds. For a chart citation this is Week 1's Claim.value and may be None — findings.md F-57: a record with no usable name is cited as nameless and renders UNVERIFIED, never under a placeholder. For a document or guideline citation it is what is actually on the page, and may not be None: a citation that quotes nothing cites nothing.
quote_or_value.title: Quote Or Value

bbox.description: Where on the page the quoted text sits. Document sources only — D3 makes the deterministic locate step the only source of a bbox, and neither a chart nor a guideline has pixels to point at. Present on an illegible field too, where it marks the ink region; a bbox alone does not make a value located (see ExtractedField).

extraction_id.description: Which extraction run produced this value. Required for document sources and forbidden for the others. D1 puts this id, alone, into procedure_result.comments; the write-back ledger maps it to document id, page and bbox.
extraction_id.title: Extraction Id

Citation.title: Citation

Comparator.description:
The censoring a lab report prints in front of a number. Values match
FHIR's `Quantity.comparator` value set, because a written-back result
surfaces as `Observation.valueQuantity` (D1, spike §5).
Comparator.title: Comparator

DocumentChecksums.description: See the module docstring: two algorithms, two fields, never compared.

sha3_512.description: OpenEMR's digest of the stored file, lowercase hex. Required before anything can be written back: it is the document half of D1's idempotency key.
sha3_512.title: Sha3 512

sha256.description: The doc-factory's digest (`document.sha256` in a ground truth file), lowercase hex. Evaluation provenance only; never used for deduplication.
sha256.title: Sha256

DocumentChecksums.title: DocumentChecksums

DocumentKind.description:
The two document kinds Week 2 extracts. Closed, because the supervisor
routes on it and the write-back path accepts exactly one of them: D2
forbids intake data reaching the chart, and the type is where that is
enforced (`LabWriteBackRequest` takes LAB_PDF and nothing else).
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

DocumentPatientHeader.description:
Who the document says it is about.

Every field is an `ExtractedField`, including the name: a scanned intake
form can have an illegible patient name, and the schema has to be able
to say so rather than emit a plausible one. The doc-factory exercises
exactly this — `intake-missing-allergy-006` omits `patient.dob`
entirely and renders `patient.city_state_zip` as an unreadable smudge.

**This header is not an identity assertion.** It is what the page says,
and matching it to a chart is a discrepancy check
(app/models/w2/intake_form.py), never a merge. Which patient a document
belongs to is decided by the upload, not by reading the paper.

date_of_birth.description: As written on the page, not parsed. Intake forms and lab reports disagree about format (the factory emits `1959-12-28` on one and `09/10/2026` on the other) and normalising here would put a parser between the page and the citation's quote.

mrn.description: Lab reports print one; intake forms generally do not.

DocumentPatientHeader.title: DocumentPatientHeader

value.description: What the document says. Non-None for located and unlocated; None for missing and illegible, where nothing was read. Read it through as_presented_fact(), not directly.

citation.description: The document citation supporting `value`; see the status rules.

confidence.description: The extractor's confidence in `value`, when it reports one. Must be None where `value` is None: a confidence about nothing is a number that invites being compared to a threshold.
confidence.title: Confidence

FieldStatus.description: What the three-stage extraction (D3) concluded about one field.
FieldStatus.title: FieldStatus

LabOrderHeader.description:
The order block — factory paths `order.*`.

Timestamps are `ExtractedField[datetime]` and parsed by the extractor,
not by this schema: a date that could not be parsed is `unlocated`, not
a silently shifted one. `LabResult.collection_date` carries the date the
idempotency key uses, at day resolution, because that is what D1's
UNIQUE key is over.
LabOrderHeader.title: LabOrderHeader

LabResult.description:
One row of a lab report.

`test_key` and `panel` come from where the row sits on the page (the
factory encodes both in its field paths, `results.<panel>.<test>.*`) and
are the schema's stable handle on the row. `test_name` is what was
printed, which is a different thing and can itself be illegible.

`loinc_code` is optional and is *not* extracted from the page: lab PDFs
rarely print one, and the write-back path needs it
(`procedure_order_code.procedure_code`, spike §9). Whatever assigns it
is a coding step outside this contract; a result without one simply
cannot be written back, which `LabWriteBackResult` enforces by requiring
it.

panel.description: Panel the row sits under, e.g. `cmp`, `lipid`, `a1c`. None when ungrouped.
panel.title: Panel

test_key.description: Stable handle for the row within this document, e.g. `glucose`.
test_key.title: Test Key

collection_date.description: The date this specimen was collected — the third component of D1's idempotency key. Usually copied from the order header; on reports that date rows individually, from the row.

reported_flag.description: What the document's flag column says, parsed by `lab_values.parse_reported_flag`. A `ReportedFlag`, not an `AbnormalFlag`: a blank column is `not_reported`, never `normal` (D20). Never the computed flag — keeping the two apart is the whole point of the cross-check.

loinc_code.description: Assigned, not extracted. See the class docstring.
loinc_code.title: Loinc Code

LabResult.title: LabResult

comparator.description: None for an exact reading; set for a censored one such as `<5`.

QualitativeLabValue.description: A term rather than a number: `positive`, `not detected`, `trace`.
QualitativeLabValue.title: QualitativeLabValue

ReferenceRange.description:
The interval a result is judged against.

`low`/`high` are the machine-comparable form; `text` is what the report
actually printed, kept verbatim because it is what a citation quotes and
because plenty of ranges (`Negative`, `See note`) have no numeric form
at all. At least one of the three is required — an all-None reference
range is an extraction bug wearing a valid object's clothes.

text.description: The range exactly as printed, e.g. `70 - 99` or `Negative`.
text.title: Text

unit.description: The unit the bounds are in.
unit.title: Unit

ReferenceRange.title: ReferenceRange

ReportedFlag.description:
What a lab report's flag column says — including the two ways it says
nothing this contract can compare against.

Separate from `AbnormalFlag` on purpose. `AbnormalFlag` is a conclusion
about a result; `ReportedFlag` is an observation about a column on a
page, and a column can be blank or illegible in ways a conclusion
cannot. Collapsing them is what let a blank column become an assertion
of normality (D12, superseded by D20).
ReportedFlag.title: ReportedFlag

SourceDocument.description:
The file an extraction is about. Identifiers and counts only — no page
text, no extracted values (CLAUDE.md invariant 1 governs what may be
logged, and this model is the thing most likely to end up in a log
line, so it holds nothing that could not).

document_id.description: Our id for the stored document. Where OpenEMR holds it this is the stringified `documents.id`, which the custom write-back endpoint returns (D1) because the standard upload API returns only `true` (spike §9).
document_id.title: Document Id

mime_type.description: Validate by content before upload: OpenEMR silently rejects a type outside `files_white_list` as an empty 404 (spike §10.6).
mime_type.title: Mime Type

has_text_layer.description: Whether stage 1 of D3 found a text layer (PyMuPDF) or had to OCR. Recorded because it is the single best predictor of `unlocated` fields, and a run's unlocated rate is meaningless without it.
has_text_layer.title: Has Text Layer

SourceDocument.title: SourceDocument

SourceType.description:
The three kinds of source a Week 2 claim can cite. Disjoint by
construction — CLAUDE.md invariant 3: "Patient-record facts and
guideline evidence are distinct source_types. Never let a guideline
citation stand in for a chart fact, or the reverse."
SourceType.title: SourceType

description:
A whole lab report, extracted.

`results` may be empty. An extraction that found no rows is a real
outcome — a scan too degraded to read is exactly the `scanned_heavy`
case the doc-factory generates — and the contract represents it as zero
presentable facts rather than refusing to exist, so the "still
processing / nothing found" states stay distinguishable (D7).

extraction_id.description: The run that produced this. Every citation below repeats it, so a value carries its provenance even after it is separated from the extraction it came from (D1).
extraction_id.title: Extraction Id
